cards.meaningVi: đổi mới, sáng tạo ra cách làm mới
cards.definitionEn: to introduce new ideas or methods
cards.example: Small companies often innovate faster than large organisations with many layers of management.
cards.cloze: Firms that fail to ___ risk losing their customers to rivals.
cards.confusables: invent (create something completely new)

cards.definitionEn: to put something into something else
cards.example: Please insert the key into the lock and turn it slowly to the left.
cards.cloze: Students ___ the missing words into each gap in the text.
cards.confusables: include (make something part of a larger group)

cards.definitionEn: to become involved in a situation to change it
cards.example: The government may intervene when prices rise too quickly for ordinary families to manage.
cards.cloze: Teachers should ___ early if students begin to fall behind.
cards.confusables: interfere (become involved in a harmful or unwanted way)

cards.definitionEn: to separate something or someone from other people or things
cards.example: Scientists isolate the virus in the laboratory to study its structure safely in detail.
cards.cloze: It is difficult to ___ one single cause of the problem.
cards.confusables: separate (divide into different parts or groups)

cards.meaningVi: truyền thông, phương tiện thông tin đại chúng
cards.definitionEn: the main ways of communicating with large numbers of people
cards.example: The media reported the election results within minutes of the final count being announced.
cards.cloze: Social ___ influence how teenagers see the world around them today.
cards.confusables: press (newspapers and journalists only)

cards.meaningVi: cách thức, chế độ, phương thức
cards.definitionEn: a way of doing something or behaving
cards.example: The train is a cheap mode of transport for students travelling between the two cities.
cards.cloze: Switch the phone to silent ___ during the examination this morning.
cards.confusables: method (a planned way of doing something)

cards.meaningVi: khuôn mẫu tư duy, mô hình mẫu
cards.definitionEn: a typical example or model of something
cards.example: The discovery created a new paradigm for understanding how the brain processes language daily.
cards.cloze: This theory challenges the old ___ that dominated economics for decades.
cards.confusables: model (a copy or example used for study)

cards.definitionEn: something that happens or exists and can be observed
cards.example: The northern lights are a natural phenomenon that attracts visitors to Norway every winter.
cards.cloze: Urban heat is a growing ___ in large modern cities worldwide.
cards.confusables: event (something that happens at a particular time)

cards.meaningVi: sự ưu tiên, điều được ưu tiên
cards.definitionEn: something that is more important than other things
cards.example: Improving safety in schools is the main priority for the city council this year.
cards.cloze: Health should be your first ___ when planning the long trip.
cards.confusables: preference (something you like more than others)

cards.definitionEn: to officially stop something by law or rule
cards.example: New rules prohibit smoking inside all public buildings in the country from next January.
cards.cloze: The school rules ___ mobile phones during lessons and examinations.
cards.confusables: ban (stop something officially, similar meaning)

cards.definitionEn: a book or magazine that is printed and sold
cards.example: The journal is a monthly publication read by doctors and researchers around the world.
cards.cloze: The ___ of the report was delayed by two weeks.
cards.confusables: edition (one version of a book or newspaper)

cards.definitionEn: to repeat the exact words that someone else said
cards.example: Students often quote famous writers at the start of their essays to introduce the topic.
cards.cloze: Please ___ your sources clearly at the end of the essay.
cards.confusables: cite (mention a source as evidence formally)

cards.meaningVi: phát hành; thả ra, giải phóng
cards.definitionEn: to let something go or make it available
cards.example: The company will release its new phone model in September at a lower starting price.
cards.cloze: Officials plan to ___ the results early on Monday morning.
cards.confusables: publish (make information available to the public)

cards.definitionEn: to change something to the opposite direction or position
cards.example: The committee decided to reverse its earlier decision after hearing complaints from local residents.
cards.cloze: Drivers must ___ carefully out of the narrow parking space.
cards.confusables: opposite (completely different, as a noun or adjective)

cards.definitionEn: to create conditions that imitate a real situation
cards.example: Pilots train in machines that simulate real flying conditions before they carry any passengers.
cards.cloze: Modern computers can ___ the effects of climate change accurately.
cards.confusables: imitate (copy the way something behaves or looks)

cards.definitionEn: only one of something
cards.example: She was the sole survivor of the accident and later described what had happened.
cards.cloze: The ___ aim of the course is to improve academic writing.
cards.confusables: single (one only, used for counting)

cards.definitionEn: a little, to some degree
cards.example: The new plan is somewhat cheaper than the old one but offers fewer services overall.
cards.cloze: His answer was ___ unclear, so the teacher explained it again.
cards.confusables: slightly (a little, used with adjectives and verbs)

cards.definitionEn: to give a document to someone in authority
cards.example: Students must submit their applications before the end of March to be considered this year.
cards.cloze: Please ___ the completed form to the office before Friday.
cards.confusables: hand in (give school work to a teacher, informal)

cards.meaningVi: người kế nhiệm, người kế tiếp
cards.definitionEn: a person who takes a job after someone else
cards.example: The director retired in June and her successor took over the department the following month.

cards.confusables: replacement (a person or thing that takes another place)

cards.definitionEn: a long piece of writing for a university degree
cards.example: She spent three years writing her thesis on the history of public health in Britain.

cards.confusables: essay (a shorter piece of writing on one subject)

cards.definitionEn: a subject that people write or talk about
cards.example: Climate change was the main topic of discussion at the conference held in Geneva.

cards.confusables: subject (an area of study at school or university)

cards.definitionEn: to send something from one place to another

cards.definitionEn: final, happening at the end of a process

cards.confusables: final (last, coming at the very end)

cards.meaningVi: độc nhất, duy nhất vô nhị
cards.definitionEn: being the only one of its kind

cards.cloze: The island is home to a ___ species of small bird.
cards.confusables: special (different or better than usual)

cards.definitionEn: able to be seen
cards.example: The mountains were clearly visible from the hotel window on the bright winter morning.

cards.confusables: obvious (easy to see or understand)

cards.definitionEn: done by choice, without being forced or paid
cards.example: Many students do voluntary work at weekends to gain experience and help their local community.

cards.definitionEn: to leave something or someone completely
cards.example: The sailors had to abandon the ship when it began to sink in the storm.

cards.definitionEn: to go somewhere with someone
cards.example: Parents often accompany their children on the first day of primary school each September.

cards.confusables: escort (go with someone to protect or guide them)

cards.definitionEn: to collect a large amount of something over time

cards.definitionEn: having more than one possible meaning

cards.definitionEn: extra material added at the end of a book

cards.meaningVi: đánh giá cao; cảm kích, biết ơn
cards.definitionEn: to understand the value or importance of something
cards.example: Visitors appreciate the museum more when guides explain the history behind each object clearly.

cards.definitionEn: based on personal choice rather than a system

cards.confusables: random (chosen without any plan or pattern)

cards.definitionEn: to make a process work by machine without people
cards.example: Factories automate simple tasks so that workers can focus on quality and safety checks.

cards.definitionEn: an unfair preference for one group or idea
cards.example: The study tried to avoid bias by including people from many different age groups.

cards.confusables: prejudice (an unfair opinion formed without knowledge)

cards.definitionEn: a drawing that shows information in a clear way

cards.confusables: graph (a drawing with lines showing changing values)

cards.definitionEn: to make something easier to understand
cards.example: The teacher used a diagram to clarify the difference between the two similar grammar points.

cards.confusables: explain (describe something so people understand it)

cards.definitionEn: a product that can be bought and sold
cards.example: Coffee is an important commodity for farmers in several mountain regions of the country.

cards.meaningVi: bổ sung, bổ trợ cho nhau
cards.definitionEn: to add to something in a way that improves it

cards.definitionEn: belonging to the present time

cards.meaningVi: mâu thuẫn với; nói ngược lại

cards.meaningVi: then chốt, cực kỳ quan trọng

cards.definitionEn: the money used in a particular country

cards.definitionEn: to be a sign of something
cards.example: Red lines on the map denote the main roads used by buses and emergency vehicles.
cards.cloze: A star on the chart will ___ the capital city.
cards.confusables: indicate (show or point to something)

cards.definitionEn: to notice something that is difficult to see
cards.example: New sensors can detect tiny amounts of pollution in rivers within a few minutes.
cards.cloze: Doctors use blood tests to ___ the disease at an early stage.
cards.confusables: discover (find something for the first time)

cards.definitionEn: to move away from the usual or expected way
cards.example: Drivers should not deviate from the signed route during road works in the city centre.

cards.confusables: differ (be unlike something else)

cards.meaningVi: buộc phải dời đi; chiếm chỗ
cards.definitionEn: to force people to leave their homes
cards.example: Floods displace thousands of families every year in low-lying areas near the great river.
cards.cloze: New technology may ___ some traditional jobs over time.
cards.confusables: replace (take the place of something else)

cards.definitionEn: a play for the theatre, radio or television
cards.example: Drama helps students speak with confidence and understand stories from other cultures and periods.
cards.cloze: She studies ___ and music at the local arts college.
cards.confusables: play (a story performed in a theatre)

cards.meaningVi: sau cùng, cuối cùng thì xảy ra

cards.example: After months of talks, the eventual agreement satisfied both the workers and the company owners.

cards.confusables: final (the last in a series)

cards.definitionEn: to show something publicly for people to look at
cards.example: Local artists exhibit their paintings in the town hall during the summer festival each year.
cards.cloze: The museum will ___ photographs from the nineteenth century.
cards.confusables: display (arrange something so people can see it)

cards.definitionEn: to use a situation or resource for advantage

cards.meaningVi: dao động, biến động thất thường
cards.definitionEn: to change frequently in amount or level
cards.example: Prices for fresh fish fluctuate daily depending on the weather and the size of catches.
cards.cloze: Temperatures ___ between seasons in the northern mountain villages.

cards.meaningVi: nguyên tắc hướng dẫn, chỉ dẫn
cards.definitionEn: a rule about how something should be done
cards.example: The guideline says that essays should be no longer than two thousand words in total.

cards.confusables: instruction (a detailed order about how to do something)

cards.definitionEn: to draw attention to something important
cards.example: The report highlights the need for cheaper housing in areas close to the city centre.

cards.confusables: emphasise (say something is especially important)

cards.definitionEn: suggested but not stated directly

cards.cloze: There was an ___ agreement that nobody would raise objections.

cards.meaningVi: gây ra, tạo ra; xui khiến
cards.definitionEn: to cause something to happen
cards.example: Certain chemicals induce sleep and are used in medicines for patients with serious anxiety problems.
cards.cloze: A lack of clean water can ___ headaches and tiredness.

cards.meaningVi: không thể tránh khỏi, tất yếu
cards.definitionEn: certain to happen and impossible to avoid
cards.example: With the population growing fast, change in the transport system is inevitable in coming years.
cards.cloze: Delays are ___ when so many flights share one runway.
cards.confusables: unavoidable (cannot be prevented from happening)

cards.definitionEn: basic systems such as roads, power and water supplies
cards.example: The government invested heavily in infrastructure, building new bridges, railways and power stations nationwide.
cards.cloze: Poor ___ slows economic growth in remote farming regions.
cards.confusables: facilities (buildings and equipment provided for an activity)

cards.definitionEn: to look at something carefully to check it
cards.example: Officials inspect restaurants regularly to make sure food is prepared in clean safe conditions.

cards.meaningVi: mạnh mẽ, dữ dội, căng thẳng

cards.meaningVi: thao tác khéo léo; thao túng
cards.definitionEn: to control or influence something in a skilful way
cards.example: Skilled workers manipulate the machine controls with great precision during the delicate repair process.
cards.cloze: Advertisers try to ___ consumers through emotional television images.
cards.confusables: control (have power over something or someone)

cards.meaningVi: giảm thiểu, hạ xuống mức thấp nhất
cards.definitionEn: to reduce something to the smallest possible amount
cards.example: Good design helps minimise waste during production and saves money for the whole company.
cards.cloze: Wearing a helmet can ___ the risk of serious injury.
cards.confusables: reduce (make something smaller in size or amount)

cards.definitionEn: to balance the effect of something bad
cards.example: Higher sales in Asia offset losses in Europe during the difficult trading year overall.
cards.cloze: Planting trees can ___ carbon emissions from the new factory.
cards.confusables: compensate (pay or balance for a loss)

cards.definitionEn: a section of writing starting on a new line

cards.confusables: section (one separate part of a document)

cards.definitionEn: and also, in addition to
cards.example: The hotel room costs eighty pounds, plus ten pounds for breakfast for two people daily.
cards.cloze: Two ___ two equals four in this basic arithmetic problem.
cards.confusables: in addition (extra, more formal phrase)

cards.meaningVi: người hành nghề, người thực hành chuyên môn
cards.definitionEn: a person who works in a particular profession
cards.example: A medical practitioner must update their knowledge regularly throughout a long career in healthcare.

cards.meaningVi: chiếm ưu thế, nổi bật nhất

cards.definitionEn: the possibility that something will happen in future

cards.confusables: outlook (the likely future situation)

cards.meaningVi: triệt để, căn bản; cấp tiến

cards.example: The new director introduced radical changes to the way the hospital organised its emergency services.

cards.definitionEn: chosen without any plan or pattern

cards.cloze: Winners are chosen in a ___ draw held each week.
cards.confusables: arbitrary (based on personal choice, not a system)

cards.definitionEn: to make something stronger or more effective

cards.meaningVi: khôi phục, phục hồi, trùng tu

cards.meaningVi: sửa lại, xét lại; ôn tập

cards.definitionEn: a plan of activities with their times

cards.cloze: Trains run according to a strict ___ throughout the day.
cards.confusables: timetable (a list of times for lessons or transport)

cards.definitionEn: nervous and unable to relax
cards.example: The atmosphere in the waiting room was tense before the examination results were finally announced.
cards.cloze: She felt ___ before speaking in front of the whole class.
cards.confusables: nervous (worried about something that will happen)

cards.definitionEn: to bring something to an end
cards.example: The company may terminate the contract if the work is not finished on time.
cards.cloze: The late train will ___ at the central station tonight.
cards.confusables: end (finish or cause something to finish)

cards.definitionEn: the main subject of a book, film or talk

cards.cloze: Love is a common ___ in popular songs and films.
cards.confusables: topic (a subject people talk or write about)

cards.meaningVi: nhờ đó, qua đó, do đó

cards.meaningVi: đồng nhất, thống nhất, đều nhau

cards.meaningVi: phương tiện giao thông, xe cộ

cards.confusables: transport (the system of moving people and goods)

cards.definitionEn: through, by way of

cards.definitionEn: almost, very nearly

cards.meaningVi: thuộc về thị giác, bằng hình ảnh
cards.definitionEn: relating to seeing and sight

cards.cloze: The design relies on strong ___ effects throughout the building.
cards.confusables: visible (able to be seen)

cards.meaningVi: lan rộng, phổ biến rộng rãi

cards.example: There is widespread support for the plan to protect forests along the northern river banks.

cards.confusables: common (happening often or found in many places)

cards.meaningVi: chứa được, đủ chỗ cho; cung cấp chỗ ở
cards.definitionEn: to provide enough space for someone or something
cards.example: The new lecture hall can accommodate up to four hundred students for special university events.

cards.confusables: house (provide a place for people to live)

cards.meaningVi: sự tương đồng, phép loại suy

cards.example: The teacher used an analogy between the heart and a pump to explain blood circulation.

cards.confusables: comparison (looking at how things are similar or different)

cards.definitionEn: to expect something to happen and prepare for it

cards.confusables: expect (think something will probably happen)

cards.meaningVi: cam đoan, đảm bảo với ai

cards.definitionEn: to succeed in achieving something after effort

cards.meaningVi: thay mặt, nhân danh, vì lợi ích của

cards.meaningVi: phần lớn, phần chủ yếu; khối lớn

cards.confusables: majority (more than half of a group)

cards.definitionEn: to stop happening or doing something

cards.meaningVi: tính mạch lạc, tính liên kết chặt chẽ

cards.confusables: unity (the state of being joined as one)

cards.meaningVi: trùng hợp, xảy ra cùng lúc

cards.meaningVi: hình dung, nghĩ ra, thai nghén ý tưởng
cards.definitionEn: to imagine or think of an idea or plan
cards.example: Architects conceive new buildings first as rough sketches before detailed plans are drawn up later.
